en.1: Fig. 1. Derivation of instruction examples and construction of the training set. a, The six groups shown here account for all 392,764 examples derived from the corpus across 13 tasks. The independent glossary supplies a further 107 examples, bringing the total to 392,871. In each paired node task, a label is either read from the XML or assigned in context; POS targets include punctuation, and constituent targets include function-word positions. b, The fixed 1,200 test records contain 1,100 distinct sentence texts, which match 1,381 source records. Excluding all matches leaves 3,635 records, from which the corpus-derived training tasks are regenerated; the four training files contain 15,742 examples.
en.2: Fig. 2. From annotated structures to instruction targets. a, Grammatical decisions recorded in the human annotations. b, Spans, labels and attributes in the reference XML provide the evidence for the corpus-derived tasks. Rules derive local single-core structures. c, Clause-, word- and constituent-level tasks supervise individual analyses. In the main task (M0), templates express these analyses in a fixed order and pair them with the reference XML. Supervised fine-tuning (SFT) combines these corpus-derived examples with the two glossary tasks.
en.3: Fig. 3. Task sizes in the complete instruction resource and the training set. a, Full collection (392,871 examples; logarithmic axis). b, Training set (15,742 examples; linear axis). After all source records matching a test sentence text were excluded, the training set comprises 3,635 whole-sentence examples, 1,000 examples from each of 12 corpus-derived auxiliary tasks, and 54 and 53 glossary examples. Colors distinguish corpus-derived auxiliary tasks (blue), glossary tasks (gray) and the main task M0 (orange); bar labels give counts. Task IDs follow Tables 3–5.
en.4: Fig. 4. Access to the study materials and reconstruction of the training set. a, Zenodo distributes the instruction files, GitHub provides the code, scores and model outputs, and the LDC distributes the source treebank. b, The main-task XML yields the 5,016 sentence–XML pairs, and the saved selection index identifies the 1,200 test records in order. Excluding all 1,381 records whose texts match the test sample leaves 3,635 records for task generation. The training set combines the resulting main-task examples, sampled auxiliary examples and the 107 glossary examples.
en.5: Fig. 5. Target-response length distributions and supervision formats. a, Quantile intervals of output-field length for each task. Whisker ends mark the 10th and 90th percentiles, boxes span the 25th to 75th percentiles and dark vertical lines mark medians, which are also listed on the right. The main task (M0) is highlighted in orange. Lengths are measured in Unicode code points on a logarithmic axis; quantiles use linear interpolation. b, Of the 392,871 instruction examples, 210,049 (53.47%) contain an explanation before the answer and 182,822 (46.53%) give a direct answer.
en.6: Fig. 6. Structural-attribute distributions in sentence-level target XML. a, Occurrences of the eight scp values. V denotes a predicate core without an object or complement, and VOCC a predicate core with one object and two complements. b, Occurrences of the eight raw fun values, with uppercase and lowercase forms counted separately. c, The ten most frequent mod patterns and their relation categories; “-” denotes other lexical relations. Counts are based on the final XML of the 5,016 main-task examples, in which scp, fun and mod occur 17,240, 5,325 and 10,941 times, respectively. Panels a and b use logarithmic axes, on which a count of 1 appears as a short mark; panel c uses a linear axis. The ten most frequent of the 593 mod patterns account for 5,177 occurrences.
en.7: Fig. 7. Evaluation under six model and fine-tuning conditions. Qwen2.5 denotes Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct and Qwen3 denotes Qwen3-4B; “No task SFT” denotes a model without project-specific fine-tuning. Qwen3 is compared before and after SFT separately with thinking disabled and enabled. a, XML parsability. b, Proportion of outputs that are both parsable and text-consistent with the original sentence. Both panels use all 1,200 inputs per condition as the denominator. c–e, Component F1 scores for Qwen2.5 (c) and for Qwen3 with thinking disabled (d) and enabled (e); n gives the number of parsable predictions before/after SFT (831/1,116, 739/999 and 905/1,137), including text-inconsistent predictions. f, Exact-match rate of linear sentence-pattern expressions over all 1,200 inputs; outputs that cannot be compared count as nonmatches, and expressions are regenerated from the reference and predicted XML before comparison. Gray bars, no task SFT; blue bars, after SFT. Bar-end labels give percentages.

zh.1: 图1 指令样本的派生与训练集构建。a，六组计数概括13类语料派生任务，共392,764条样本；独立符号释义表另提供107条，两者合计392,871条。配对的节点任务分别要求解读XML中的标记，或根据语境判断标签；词类目标含标点，成分目标含虚词位。b，固定的1,200条测试记录含1,100种不同整句文本，在源语料中匹配1,381条记录。排除全部匹配记录后，从其余3,635条记录重新生成语料派生任务；四份训练文件共含15,742条样本。
zh.2: 图2 从标注结构到指令任务的目标答案。a，人工标注中记录的语法判断。b，参考XML中的片段、标签和属性为各项语料派生任务提供依据，单核结构由规则派生。c，小句、词和成分层面的任务分别监督局部分析；整句主任务M0按固定顺序用模板表述这些分析，并与参考XML共同构成目标答案。监督微调（SFT）使用这些语料派生样本及两类符号释义样本。
zh.3: 图3 完整指令资源与训练集的任务规模。a，完整资源共392,871条样本，采用对数横轴。b，训练集共15,742条样本，采用线性横轴。排除与测试整句文本相同的全部源记录后，训练集由3,635条整句主任务样本、12类语料派生辅助任务各1,000条样本，以及两类符号释义样本（54条、53条）组成。蓝色表示语料派生辅助任务，灰色表示符号释义任务，橙色表示主任务M0；条末标出计数，任务编号见表3—5。
zh.4: 图4 研究材料的获取与训练集重建。a，Zenodo提供指令文件，GitHub提供代码、评分结果和模型作答，LDC提供原始树库。b，从整句主任务的最终XML可恢复5,016条原句与XML配对，保存的抽样索引标识1,200条测试记录及其顺序。排除与测试整句文本匹配的全部1,381条记录后，保留3,635条用于生成任务。训练集由所得整句主任务样本、抽取的辅助任务样本和107条符号释义样本组成。
zh.5: 图5 目标响应长度分布与监督形式。a，各任务output字段长度的分位区间：横线端点为第10和90百分位，色块覆盖第25至75百分位，深色竖线为中位数，右侧另列中位数。主任务M0以橙色突出。长度按Unicode码点统计，横轴为对数尺度，分位数采用线性插值。b，392,871条指令样本中，210,049条（53.47%）在答案前附有说明，182,822条（46.53%）直接给出答案。
zh.6: 图6 整句目标XML的结构属性分布。a，八种scp取值的出现次数；V表示不带宾语或补语的谓核，VOCC表示带一个宾语和两个补语的谓核。b，八种fun原始取值的出现次数，大写和小写分别计数。c，频次最高的十种mod模式及其关系类别；“-”表示其他词法关系。统计对象为5,016条整句主任务的最终XML，其中scp、fun和mod分别出现17,240、5,325和10,941次。a、b采用对数横轴，计数为1的项目以短线标示；c采用线性横轴。593种mod模式中，前十种合计出现5,177次。
zh.7: 图7 六种模型与微调条件下的评测结果。Qwen2.5表示Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct，Qwen3表示Qwen3-4B；“未SFT”表示未接受本项目任务微调。Qwen3分别在思考关闭和开启时比较SFT前后的表现。a，XML可解析率。b，XML可解析且文本与原句一致的输出比例。两者均以每种条件的全部1,200条输入为分母。c—e，依次为Qwen2.5、关闭思考的Qwen3和开启思考的Qwen3的分项F1；n为SFT前后的可解析预测数（831/1,116、739/999、905/1,137），其中保留文本不一致的预测。f，全部1,200条输入的线性句式表达式完全匹配率；无法比较的输出计为未匹配，表达式从参考XML和预测XML重新生成后比较。灰色条表示未SFT，蓝色条表示SFT后，条末标签为百分比。
